title: Epoch gap mode and tooltip throttling for scrollable time-series
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Long, high-resolution time-series in the console become noisy and expensive to render and narrate when there are long temporal gaps in the data (days/weeks with no points). Current tooltips render full DOM popovers per point and the screen reader announces every hovered datapoint which leads to poor performance and noisy a11y output for customers.
proposed_solution: Introduce an 'epoch gap mode' visual treatment and interaction pattern that: 1) collapses long empty spans into a condensed gap band with a subtle token-driven treatment; 2) surfaces a concise summary for collapsed epochs (count of missing intervals, estimated bucket span) using a single accessible node; 3) throttle and simplify tooltip output by default (condensed, single-line summaries with debounce) and provide explicit expand interactions for full details. Implement progressive hydration: lightweight DOM for summarized regions and on-demand richer DOM only when users request details.
acceptance_criteria: When a continuous time span exceeds configured threshold (default 72h of no points) render a collapsed gap band with a 'gap-summary' token;
Hover/keyboard-focus over collapsed band shows a single concise tooltip (title + one-line summary) with 200-400ms debounce;
Tabbing through the series lands on summarized nodes only (not every missing slot) and screen reader announces a succinct line per collapsed region;
Full detail must be reachable via keyboard (Enter or Space) to open expanded panel with original point-level details;
Rendering cost for a 10k-point timeline with 5 large gaps reduces main-thread paint and layout time by >= 35% in our lab harness;
WCAG 2.1 AA maintained: contrasts meet tokens, keyboard operable, and screen reader flow is not degraded for sighted users relying on assistive tech;
Design tokens added for gap band color, collapsed-summary text, and tooltip compact variants, and documented in tokens docs.
design_notes: Tokens: propose new tokens - color.timeseries.gap, token.timeseries.gap-contrast, token.tooltip.condensed-bg, token.tooltip.condensed-typography;
Visual: collapsed gap should use 2px dashed lower-opacity edge and 1.5x height of baseline series to stay visible but not compete with series lines;
Interaction: concise tooltip shows count + start/end dates and an affordance ‘Expand for points’ with keyboard hint; long press on touch expands;
Accessibility: screen reader mode announces 'Collapsed gap, X days missing, press Enter for details' and focus lands on the collapsed band; avoid per-point announcement on collapse;
Motion: no animations longer than 120ms for collapse/expand to avoid jank on low-power devices; prefer opacity fade + transform translateY(4px) for expansion.
engineering_notes: Implementation approach: canvas-based line rendering + overlayed lightweight DOM hit targets for collapsed bands; full DOM for expanded details;
Performance: use off-main frame bitmap caching for unchanged line segments; reuse KV cache for time-range aggregates used by summaries;
API: add chart prop 'epochGapThresholdMs' and 'gapBandToken' to allow host components to configure;
Telemetry: emit events for 'gap-collapsed', 'gap-expanded', and 'tooltip-condensed-shown' with sampling to track usage and error rates;
Rollout: behind feature flag 'timeseries-gap-mode', canary to 10% of orgs for 2 weeks, then 50% while monitoring render/latency.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: We prefer condensed tooltips to reduce DOM churn and SR verbosity; tradeoff is potential discoverability loss — mitigated with explicit 'Expand for points' affordance and keyboard hints.
Canvas rendering improves paint performance but complicates text selection and copy; we will surface copy via expanded panel where DOM exists.
Default threshold set to 72h but configurable per-chart; conservative to avoid collapsing short weekend gaps unexpectedly.
